analysis.summary: The PR introduces architectural changes to split BFF routes into public and private handlers, but fails to update the tRPC client to use separate endpoints, and removes critical CloudFront URL rewriting logic without ensuring S3 objects match the new URL paths.

bugs.title: tRPC client calls private procedures on public endpoint
bugs.description: The tRPC client is configured with a single URL and typed as AppRouter & PrivateRouter, but the backend now exposes AppRouter and PrivateRouter as separate handlers at different URL paths (/__app__/... vs /__app-private__/...). When the client attempts to call private procedures (getCartModel, deleteEntry, etc.), they will be sent to the public handler which does not have these procedures registered, causing runtime errors.
bugs.risk: All private BFF operations (cart mutations, entry management) will fail at runtime with 'procedure not found' errors because the client targets the wrong handler.

bugs.title: CloudFront path stripping removal breaks static site routing
bugs.description: The removed CloudFront Function (cfFunction) was stripping the base path (/__app__/name/target) from incoming requests before forwarding to S3, and appending .html/index.html for clean URLs. Without this rewrite, requests to /__app__/name/target/ will look for an S3 object at key '__app__/name/target/' instead of 'index.html', and /page routes will 404 instead of serving page.html. The webpack output places index.html at the bucket root, not under the prefixed path.
bugs.risk: All static HTML pages will return 404 errors because CloudFront requests S3 objects using the full URL path including the /__app__/ prefix, but the files are stored at the bucket root.

notBugs.reason: The removal of pathRewrite in webpack.config.web-app.ts is correct because the BffApi.ts changes updated the API Gateway routes to accept the full path including the /__app__/ prefix, so rewriting is no longer needed.
Splitting the tRPC router into public and private handlers is an intentional architectural change, not a bug in itself (though the client implementation to support it is broken).
